item.title: John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell on ‘Wild Horse Nine’
item.description: The longtime friends talk about sinister characters and the politics that underpin the C.I.A. story at the heart of their new darkly comic drama, “Wild Horse Nine.”
item.dc:creator: Clarissa Cruz
item.media:credit: Trent Davis Bailey for The New York Times
item.media:description: “Sam is an actor who isn’t at all pretentious and isn’t at all precious, but has a great work ethic, takes it very seriously and conversely loves to have fun doing it,” Malkovich, left, said of his co-star Rockwell. “And I think those two different facets need to go together.”

item.title: Toronto International Film Festival Tries Adding a Market

item.title: ‘Woman Unknown’ Takes Top Prize at Venice Film Festival
item.description: The film, a drama directed by May el-Toukhy, follows a Danish servant in the uneasy years after World War II. Lee Chang-dong’s “Possible Love” won the runner-up award.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Rapold
item.media:description: The director May el-Toukhy receiving the Golden Lion Award for her film “Woman Unknown” at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival on Saturday.

item.title: Jacob Tremblay Plays Young Ted Kaczynski in Netflix’s ‘Unabomber’
item.description: A decade ago, he made a name for himself as a young actor in “Room” and “Wonder.” But Tremblay is ready for his next chapter.
item.dc:creator: Ashley Spencer
item.media:credit: Alana Paterson for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jacob Tremblay said that acting as a child wasn’t harmful to him. “If anything, from a young age, it taught me in the real world to be really empathetic and be really in touch with my feelings,” he said.
